story.iWant: I want to define roles, enforce permissions, and invite users via email
story.soThat: So that API/UX only exposes functions allowed by user's assigned role, and I can securely onboard new users to the correct company with the appropriate role.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: User entity includes a `role` field with validation: must be one of `admin`, `accountant`, `chief_accountant`, or `cfo` (case-sensitive lowercase). Existing users without a role must be assigned a default role (default: `accountant`).
Permission matrix defined and documented (API + UI): which endpoints/resources each role can access. Documentation must include OpenAPI/Swagger annotations and a written permission matrix document.

Middleware checks JWT and role on each API request; 403 Forbidden returned with context-aware error message (e.g., "Access denied. Required role: ADMIN" or "Only ADMIN or CHIEF_ACCOUNTANT can perform this action"). Requests with missing or invalid role in JWT return 401 Unauthorized.

UI hides menu items/screens based on role, but API rejects unauthorized backend access regardless of UI. If a user manually navigates to an unauthorized page (e.g., via URL), the frontend displays a 403 error page.

All role/permission changes are logged in audit trail with: old_role, new_role, changed_by_user_id, target_user_id, timestamp, and IP address. Logging occurs before the change is applied (failure to log blocks the change).

Changing one's own role is not permitted (only admin/chief can edit others). System returns 403 Forbidden with message: "You cannot change your own role" when user attempts self-role-change. Validation enforced at both API and UI levels.
Role field validation: Invalid role values are rejected with 400 Bad Request error. Role validation occurs during user creation, user update, and role assignment operations.
Role assignment during user creation: New users must be assigned a valid role (default: `accountant` if not specified). Admin or chief_accountant can specify role during user creation.

JWT token includes role claim: All JWT access tokens must include the user's role in the token claims. Token refresh preserves role claim. If role is missing from token, authentication fails with 401 Unauthorized.

Spring Security context includes role: After JWT validation, user's role is available in Spring Security context for use in @PreAuthorize annotations. Role is extracted from JWT and set as authority (e.g., `ROLE_ADMIN`, `ROLE_ACCOUNTANT`).

User invitation system: Admin or chief_accountant can invite users via email instead of creating accounts directly. Invitation includes unique token, company association, and expiration (7 days). Invited users can register via invitation link, which validates token, pre-fills email, and automatically associates user with company and assigned role.

Invitation email delivery: System sends invitation emails to invited users containing invitation link, inviter information, company name, and expiration details. Uses existing EmailService (Resend) for email delivery.

Invitation acceptance flow: Public invitation acceptance page validates token, checks expiration, allows user registration (password, name), creates user account with correct company and role, and marks invitation as accepted.
Invitation audit trail: All invitation actions (create, accept, expire) are logged in audit trail with: inviter, invitee email, company, status, timestamp, and IP address.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: Defines four roles: Admin (Technical), Accountant, Chief Accountant, and CFO with clear permission boundaries. System must enforce role-based permissions at API level.

doc.title: Decision Architecture
doc.snippet: JWT authentication with Spring Security 6. Uses Spring Security filter chain for JWT validation. Method-level security patterns for role-based authorization.

doc.title: User Registration & Secure Authentication
doc.snippet: Establishes JWT authentication pattern. User entity already includes role field (String). JwtTokenProvider generates tokens with role claim. JwtAuthenticationFilter extracts user from JWT. SecurityConfig configures Spring Security filter chain.

artifact.reason: User entity already has role field (String, line 29) that needs validation. Implements CompanyScopedEntity for multi-tenancy. Role field exists but lacks validation constraint.

JWT token provider already includes role in token generation (generateAccessToken method accepts role parameter). Need to verify role is extracted from User and passed correctly. getRoleFromToken method exists (line 83-86).
JWT authentication filter extracts role from token (line 37) and sets as authority with ROLE_ prefix (line 41). Authority format needs to match Spring Security @PreAuthorize hasRole checks.

Spring Security configuration needs to enable method security (@EnableMethodSecurity) for role-based endpoint protection using @PreAuthorize annotations. Currently only configures basic JWT filter chain.
Audit service interface needs to be extended with methods for logging role changes (ROLE_CHANGED action) and invitation operations (INVITATION_CREATED, INVITATION_ACCEPTED, INVITATION_EXPIRED).
REST controller pattern to follow for UserController and InvitationController. Shows authentication endpoint structure and error handling patterns. Uses JwtTokenProvider for token generation.
Email service interface needs to be extended with sendInvitationEmail method following the pattern from sendPasswordResetEmail. Uses Resend email service for delivery.

constraints.constraint: User entity already has role field (String) from Story 1.3. Convert String role to Role enum for type safety while keeping String in database for flexibility. Add validation to ensure String values match enum values.
JWT token provider already includes role in token generation (generateAccessToken method accepts role parameter). Verify role is extracted from User entity and passed correctly to token generation.
JWT authentication filter extracts role from token but needs to properly set authority format as ROLE_ADMIN, ROLE_ACCOUNTANT, etc. to match Spring Security @PreAuthorize hasRole checks.
Follow Spring Security 6 method-level security patterns for role-based authorization. Use @PreAuthorize annotations for role-based endpoint protection (e.g., @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")).
Role enum values: ADMIN, ACCOUNTANT, CHIEF_ACCOUNTANT, CFO (database stores lowercase: admin, accountant, chief_accountant, cfo). Spring Security authorities format: ROLE_ADMIN, ROLE_ACCOUNTANT, etc.
Permission matrix must be documented in OpenAPI/Swagger annotations and separate documentation file. UI hiding is not a security boundary - backend must enforce all permissions.
Audit trail: All role changes must be logged with old/new role, who changed it, when, IP, and user agent. Logging must be transactional (fail if logging fails).

Role validation: Self-role-change prevention must be enforced at both API and UI levels. Error messages: 403 responses must include context-aware messages following format: { "error": { "code": "FORBIDDEN", "message": "Access denied. Required role: ADMIN" }, "meta": {...} }

Default role: New users without explicit role assignment default to 'accountant'. Role validation: Invalid role values must be rejected with 400 Bad Request (not 403). JWT token missing role: Return 401 Unauthorized (not 403) when role claim is missing from token.

User invitation pattern: Follow existing email service pattern (EmailService.sendPasswordResetEmail) for invitation emails. Invitation tokens should be secure (UUID v4, at least 32 chars). Invitation table implements CompanyScopedEntity for multi-tenancy. Public invitation endpoints (/api/v1/invitations/{token}) do not require authentication but must validate token properly.
Migration V5 needed to add CHECK constraint for valid roles and set default roles for existing users. Migration V6 needed to create invitations table with indexes and foreign keys.

ideas.idea: Test role enum validation: create user with valid role (admin, accountant, chief_accountant, cfo) - should succeed. Create user with invalid role - should fail with 400 Bad Request.
Test default role assignment: create user without role field - should default to 'accountant'. Verify existing users with NULL role are updated to 'accountant' via migration.
Test 403 responses: call protected endpoint without required role - should return 403 with message "Access denied. Required role: ADMIN". Test missing role in JWT - should return 401 Unauthorized.
Test UI visibility: login as accountant - admin menu items should be hidden. Navigate to /admin via URL as accountant - should show 403 error page.
Test audit logging: change user role - verify audit log created with old_role, new_role, changed_by_user_id, target_user_id, timestamp, IP address. Test logging failure blocks role change.
Test self-role-change prevention: attempt to change own role - should fail with 403 "You cannot change your own role". Test as non-admin attempting to change role - should fail with 403.
Test JWT role claim: verify access token includes role claim. Verify token refresh preserves role claim. Test missing role claim - authentication should fail with 401.
Test Spring Security context: after JWT validation, verify role is available in SecurityContext as ROLE_ADMIN, ROLE_ACCOUNTANT, etc. Test @PreAuthorize annotations work correctly.

Test invitation creation: admin creates invitation - should succeed and generate token. Test duplicate invitation (same email+company) - should fail with 409 Conflict. Test invitation acceptance - should create user with correct company and role.

Test invitation acceptance flow: validate token, check expiration, allow registration, create user account, mark invitation as accepted. Test expired token - should fail with 404. Test invalid token - should fail with 404.
Test invitation audit logging: verify all invitation actions (create, accept, expire) are logged with inviter, invitee email, company, status, timestamp, IP address.
